observations.statement: Firecrawl deployment mode must remain visible, silent switching between self-hosted and hosted/cloud modes is forbidden, and self-hosted operation is distinguished from hosted credit billing.

The PM WebProviderAdapterRegistry is declared the capability SSOT, with a common row shape spanning support tier, cost/cache policy, fallback rank, health, network-policy attributes, credential references, and projection state.
Users can change the global provider stack, per-operation reordering is excluded from MVP, and capability tier is explicitly separate from routing posture.
Fallback is constrained to eligible adapters for the same operation, repeats through the eligible set, and terminates with adapter_unavailable plus a failure summary when all providers fail.

Settings and help surfaces must disclose provider health/errors, last failure, contextual help, availability, and support tier; model-native rows reuse the configured provider account instead of adding a separate web-search credential silo.
The activity contract reserves Reading Site for PM-native Site Reader and assigns provider-routed fetch a distinct Fetching Site label.
Source provenance is ordered from site-reader evidence through search snippets, with snippet citations conditionally allowed only when visibly labeled and no deeper read or extract occurred.
Batch operations define per-URL provenance, one multi-domain approval prompt, URL and concurrency limits, continue-on-error behavior, and a capped timeout formula.
The cache contract uses a two-phase lookup, distinguishes adapter identity after provider selection, defines per-project LRU/TTL behavior, and supplies explicit cache and change states.
Tools owns tool-level web behavior, provider capability, Firecrawl routing, and cache routing, while storage owns persistence and activity-payload storage and other named surfaces remain consumers.
Routing research lineage names validated topic inputs and competitor baselines.
autonomous_budget_exceeded is a soft error that preserves named partial-result fields and permits agents to use those results or retry with a larger budget.

candidate_findings.title: Firecrawl deployment-mode resolution is incomplete
candidate_findings.problem: The contract forbids silent hosted/self-hosted switching and requires visible deployment mode, but configuration is described only as an API key or self-hosted URL and no active-mode precedence or transition rule is stated.
candidate_findings.consequence: When both configurations exist, implementations can select different endpoints, disclosures, and credit treatment.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: The canonical active-mode state, precedence when both configurations exist, explicit transition and failure semantics, and persistence/audit treatment are unspecified.

candidate_findings.title: Effective-provider ordering is not deterministic
candidate_findings.problem: Fallback is described as priority-ordered, while routing must also be cost-aware because static priority is insufficient and the shared resolver filters on several additional dimensions.
candidate_findings.consequence: Eligible implementations can choose different providers for the same runtime snapshot, changing cost, provenance, and fallback disclosure.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: No total ordering or tie-break precedence is defined among user priority, cost, support tier, runtime identity, execution role, auth viability, health, and freshness.

candidate_findings.title: DuckDuckGo webresearch support tier conflicts
candidate_findings.problem: One rule fixes DuckDuckGo webresearch as pm-composed, while the capability matrix stores native-ish / pm_composed and its interpretation again permits either posture.
candidate_findings.consequence: Registry projection and eligibility checks cannot derive one unambiguous stored capability tier.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: The single canonical stored tier, the conditions selecting native-ish versus pm_composed, and the representation of a dual or conditional tier are unresolved.

candidate_findings.title: Snippet-only final citation policy is internally inconsistent
candidate_findings.problem: The routing contract says final citations must come from an actual read path and raw search snippets alone are insufficient, but separately allows snippet citations when no deeper read or extract occurred.
candidate_findings.consequence: The same snippet-only answer can be accepted or rejected depending on which rule a consumer implements.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: The exact exception conditions and whether snippet-only final claims are permitted are not reconciled with the mandatory search-then-read rule.

candidate_findings.title: webfetch does not select between Site Reader and provider fetch
candidate_findings.problem: Reading intents resolve to webfetch, Site Reader requires real browser interaction, providers retain real webfetch capability, and the two execution paths have different reserved identities, but no selection condition between them is defined.
candidate_findings.consequence: Implementations can disagree on execution path, activity label, provenance badge, permission behavior, and cache behavior for the same read intent.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: Precedence between PM-native Site Reader and provider-routed webfetch, plus fallback behavior when browser interaction is unavailable, is unspecified.

candidate_findings.title: Search activity label has two canonical-looking forms
candidate_findings.problem: The canonical activity set names Searching Web: <query>, while the cited-search workflow permits either Web search: <query> or Searching Web: <query>.
candidate_findings.consequence: GUI copy, audit rows, snapshots, and acceptance checks can diverge while each follows core text.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: The status of Web search: <query> as a legacy alias, and the surfaces on which it remains allowed, are not defined.

candidate_findings.title: Credit warning and cap lack enforceable semantics
candidate_findings.problem: Routing must align with a >100 credits warning and 500 credits cap, but the core supplies no measurement scope, accounting period, unit ownership, or hard/soft enforcement behavior.
candidate_findings.consequence: Providers and clients can warn or stop at different times and against different credit totals.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: The counted credit domain, warning trigger, cap enforcement point, reset scope, and treatment of estimated versus actual charges are unspecified.

candidate_findings.title: Concurrent stop-on-first-failure behavior is underdefined
candidate_findings.problem: continue_on_error false stops on the first failure while concurrency can reach ten, but the disposition of already-running and queued URLs is not stated.
candidate_findings.consequence: Completed-result sets and child audit events can differ under the same simultaneous failures.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: In-flight cancellation or draining, queue cutoff, deterministic result ordering, and batch-status selection under concurrent failures are unspecified.

candidate_findings.title: Batch timeout formula depends on an undefined individual_timeout
candidate_findings.problem: The locked batch timeout uses individual_timeout × min(url_count, 5), capped at 600 seconds, but individual_timeout is not defined among the batch inputs and its interaction with concurrency is unstated.
candidate_findings.consequence: Equivalent batches can receive different wall-clock limits across implementations.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: The source/default of individual_timeout, timer start point, and interaction with concurrency and early-stop behavior are unspecified.

candidate_findings.title: Cache identity and multi-adapter storage semantics are incomplete
candidate_findings.problem: Pre-provider lookup uses only (url, formats_hash), post-selection validation checks adapter_id and discards a mismatch, while normalized_url, formats_hash, adapter_id, and stable key ordering are listed without construction rules.
candidate_findings.consequence: Provider-specific entries can collide, be overwritten, or produce inconsistent hits and misses.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: Canonical URL normalization, formats serialization/hash construction, multi-adapter entry layout, and selection among multiple adapter variants are unspecified.

candidate_findings.title: Soft-error result envelope is not defined
candidate_findings.problem: autonomous_budget_exceeded carries an error code alongside usable partial fields, but the enclosing operation status and required/nullability behavior are not stated.
candidate_findings.consequence: Consumers can discard partial evidence, render a hard failure, or render success inconsistently.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: The top-level status, partial-field presence rules, completion semantics, and consumer handling for this soft error are unspecified.

candidate_findings.title: Unconfigured providers have ambiguous fallback classification
candidate_findings.problem: Routing filters on auth viability and has a terminal branch for no configured provider, yet unconfigured is also named as a visible provider-fallback reason before a successful answer.
candidate_findings.consequence: Audit and UI consumers can classify the same skipped provider as pre-routing ineligibility or an attempted fallback.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: Whether unconfigured providers enter the eligible set, whether they set provider_fallback_occurred, and how their reason is ordered relative to execution failures are unspecified.

candidate_findings.title: Model-native availability composition lacks a state rule
candidate_findings.problem: Availability derives from auth state, account selection, model support, health, and configuration availability, while an unavailable status token exists without precedence or reason composition.
candidate_findings.consequence: Settings and routing can disagree about whether a model-native capability is enabled, unavailable, or unhealthy.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: A deterministic availability state transition and precedence rule across the listed inputs, including the reason exposed to users, is unspecified.

candidate_findings.title: Named validation lineage lacks acceptance assertions
candidate_findings.problem: The core lists validated topic inputs and competitor baselines but does not associate them with expected routing outcomes, assertions, or receipt identifiers.
candidate_findings.consequence: The named lineage cannot by itself establish which exact contract behaviors passed validation.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: Per-input expected behavior, pass/fail criteria, and traceable validation evidence are absent from this window.

explicit_non_gaps.statement: Global provider ordering is explicitly user-changeable, while per-operation reordering is explicitly out of MVP.
Capability tier is explicitly preserved separately from routing posture, so Site Reader primacy does not erase real provider fetch capability.
Model-native web search explicitly reuses the configured provider account and forbids a separate web-search API-key field for that account.
A capability-unavailable branch with setup guidance and an all-provider-failed adapter_unavailable result are both explicit.
PM-native Site Reader and provider-routed fetch have explicitly distinct activity identities.
Batch permission behavior explicitly uses one prompt listing every unique domain and grants the listed domains for the session.
Batch URL maxima, concurrency default and maximum, continue_on_error default, and the false branch are explicitly stated.
Requests containing actions explicitly bypass read-time cache, while final-result storage remains applicable and completion storage is conditioned on cache_policy.store.
The ownership boundary between Tools, storage, and consumer/provider-adjacent documents is explicit.
The soft-error contract explicitly preserves answer_summary, sources_used_count, and research_steps and permits use or retry.

exact_evidence_refs.exact_text: - PM MUST NOT silently switch between self-hosted Firecrawl and hosted/cloud Firecrawl

- deployment-mode disclosure remains visible
- self-hosted Firecrawl does not use hosted credit billing

- `autonomous_budget_exceeded` means autonomous research hit an iteration/time/credit cap without a satisfactory result. This is a soft error: the tool still returns partial results collected before the budget was hit, with the error code present alongside partial `answer_summary`, `sources_used_count`, and `research_steps`; agents may use the partial results or retry with a larger budget.
- status: "unavailable"
- The global provider stack is user-changeable in Settings, while per-operation priority reordering is not MVP and the MVP priority order must not be treated as immutable product policy.

- The PM WebProviderAdapterRegistry is the registry SSOT for provider and adapter capability. Active rows include Exa, Tavily, Firecrawl, Anthropic/OpenAI model-native search, Google-compatible adapters, DuckDuckGo, and coding-agent or MCP projections as adapter consumers. Direct API, MCP-server, model-native, CLI/server bridge, and PM-native adapters all project from the same registry row shape with support tier, cost/cache policy, fallback rank, health, robots support, egress policy, SSRF/private-host policy, credential refs only, and projection state.

- The provider capability matrix must preserve capability tier separately from routing posture: Firecrawl, Tavily, and Exa retain real webfetch capability and must not be flattened to fallback-only merely because Site Reader is preferred.
- DuckDuckGo capability rows must preserve native-ish search, PM-composed research/fetch/extract, and partial crawl behavior instead of flattening those cells to unsupported.

- GUI/help canon must preserve row-level health/error disclosure, last-failure messaging, inline contextual help, and availability/support-tier visibility in Settings and /web help/autocomplete. Help appears inline as a tooltip or below-field text, not as a separate help page; Settings UI, `/web` help, and autocomplete show both provider availability and support tier per provider × operation as a capability matrix or per-provider badge rows.

- Firecrawl provider identity canon includes exact provider ID firecrawl, display name Firecrawl, default lower-priority position below Exa and Tavily and above DuckDuckGo, user-adjustable ordering, default-disabled state until API key or self-hosted URL is configured, and retirement of exact stale residue "stale cited-search framing and older `newtools` wording" from owner/provider canon.
- Support-tier stored canon uses `pm_composed` for PM-assembled behavior; `pm-composed` is only a display/source-lineage alias and must normalize to `pm_composed`.

- Provider fallback on rate-limit or outage falls to the next eligible provider in priority order that supports the SAME operation; PM does NOT stop solely because one provider hit a rate-limit or outage. The fallback path is shown in BOTH the chat activity label and the audit log through `provider_fallback_summary`.

- Model-native Anthropic/OpenAI web-search availability derives from provider auth state, current-account selection, selected/effective model support, provider health, and `/configuration/availability`; PM must not expose a separate web-search-specific API key field when the provider account is already configured.
- DuckDuckGo `webresearch` is `pm-composed`
Capability tier and routing posture are separate dimensions. Site Reader primacy for `webfetch` is a routing rule, not a capability erasure.

| `webresearch` | `native-ish` | `native` | `native` | `pm_composed` | `pm_composed` | `native-ish / pm_composed` |
| `webcrawl` | `native` | `native` | `native` | `pm_composed` if PM native crawler exists | `pm_composed` if PM native crawler exists | `partial native-ish / pm_composed` |
| `webmap` | `unsupported` unless PM composes it | `native` | `native` | `pm_composed` if PM native map exists | `pm_composed` if PM native map exists | `unsupported` unless PM supplies native map |

- DuckDuckGo `websearch` is `native-ish`; DuckDuckGo `webresearch` may be native-ish through provider composition or `pm_composed`; DuckDuckGo `webfetch` / `webextract` remain PM-composed rather than flattened to `unsupported`; DDG `/extract/research` is therefore PM-composed, while DuckDuckGo crawl preserves partial native-ish `search_and_crawl` behavior or PM-composed traversal.

- Anthropic/OpenAI model-native web-search rows reuse PM's provider-account/auth model. When an Anthropic or OpenAI provider account is already configured, PM does not expose a separate web-search API key field; Settings show the provider name, enabled toggle, capability badges, effective account label, effective model, auth state, and rate-limit summary for that model-native capability.
- The web routing algorithm must include a capability-unavailable terminal branch with clear setup guidance when no provider supports the requested operation.
- Site Reader canon must require real browser interaction, reserve `Reading Site` for the PM-native Site Reader path, and prevent provider-routed fetch from reusing that reserved identity.

- Answer construction must preserve search-then-read behavior, final citations must come from the actual read path rather than raw search snippets alone, and web activity/provenance docs must use the exact storage/contracts/browser ContractRef targets instead of malformed generic anchors.

- Routing must remain cost-aware when multiple providers offer similar capability; static priority alone is insufficient, and the >100 credits warning plus 500 credits cap must remain aligned with routing.

- Natural-language web intents must hit the same dispatcher as slash commands, and site or page reading intents must resolve to webfetch rather than websearch or provider extract.
- `search_provider` override is NOT exposed as a tool parameter; provider selection is handled by the capability-based routing algorithm and configured provider stack.

- Adapter-agnostic routing follows the ordered sequence: Step 1: NORMALIZE OPERATION - normalize the requested operation/input; resolve the canonical runtime snapshot; resolve permission for the canonical web tool key; Step 5: QUERY CAPABILITY MATRIX by querying the provider capability registry / adapter contract; filter eligible adapters by runtime identity constraints, support tier, execution role, account/auth viability, and freshness/health constraints; choose the effective adapter through the shared runtime/provider resolver; fallback only to the next eligible adapter for the same operation; and persist both canonical runtime snapshot + web-operation payload.

- If provider execution fails, PM tries the next eligible same-operation adapter, records `provider_fallback_occurred` and `provider_fallback_summary`, and repeats until success or the eligible set is exhausted. If all providers fail, the operation returns `adapter_unavailable` with a summary of failures rather than a success-shaped fallback.
- The web routing recovery-plan is MVP: when no configured provider supports the requested operation, the capability-unavailable terminal branch includes clear setup guidance, provider configuration pointers, and the reason the selected route cannot proceed.

- Web activity labels are routing-aware. The canonical set is `Searching Web: <query>`, `Fetching Site: <url> (via <provider>)`, `Reading Site: <url>`, `Extracting Site: <url>`, `Researching Web: <task>`, `Crawling Site: <url>`, and `Mapping Site: <url>`; internal payloads may still store `root_url` and normalized task summaries for crawl/map/research.

- Chat-transparency requires each activity row to expose whether evidence came from search, provider/API extraction, PM-native Site Reader, research synthesis, crawl, or map; source blocks and audit rows remain source-linked and cite the actual read path. The final sources-block deduplicates repeated URLs and /mapped page sets while retaining the strongest provenance badge per source, ordered strongest to weakest as `site_reader` / `site reader`, `site_extract` / `site extract`, `research_synthesis` / `research synthesis`, `crawl_result` / `crawl result`, `map_result` / `map result`, then `search_snippet` / `search snippet`. When no deeper read or extract occurred, search-snippet citations are allowed only when visibly labeled as snippet-level provenance.
- `Reading Site: <url>` is reserved EXCLUSIVELY for the PM-native Site Reader path; provider-routed or provider-delegated fetch uses `Fetching Site: <url> (via <provider>)`.

- Cited web search (`cited-web-search`, legacy `cited-search`) is an explicit PM web workflow: show `Web search: <query>` or `Searching Web: <query>`, perform `websearch`, choose candidate sources, call `webfetch` (`/webfetch`) / `Reading Site` or Site Reader before final claims, and answer with `/citations` / sources from the actual read path. Provider-specific helper names and adapter parameters do not become PM-owned tool names.

- Provider fallback treats `/rate-limit/outage`, `/unconfigured`, and provider-specific failure as visible routing reasons, not silent product behavior; the `/product` copy and audit record disclose the effective provider, fallback reason, and setup guidance before presenting a successful answer.

- Web operation completion formats the result according to the tool output contract, computes a `change_tracking` diff when applicable, stores in cache when `cache_policy.store` is true, and records audit events with all routing metadata.
- Site Reader v1 requires real browser-interaction capability, not static HTTP fetch only

- final citations come from the actual read path
- raw search snippets alone are not enough provenance for the final answer
- cost-aware selection when providers offer similar capability
- >100 credits
- 500 credits
- cost-aware selection
- static priority alone is insufficient

- NL intents and slash commands hit the same dispatcher
- "search the web for X" → `websearch`
- "extract this page" → `webextract`
- "read this URL" → `webfetch`
- "research topic" → `webresearch`
- Reading intents MUST resolve to `webfetch`, not `websearch`

- `continue_on_error?: boolean` (default true)
- With `continue_on_error?: boolean` default true, a batch succeeds if at least one URL succeeds; setting `continue_on_error: false` stops on the first failure and returns completed results plus failure detail.
- "For Session" grants all listed domains for that session

- The PM-owned web cache contract must preserve two-phase lookup, state vocabulary, and per-project cache sizing.
- Two-phase cache-check is locked: before provider selection, PM checks `(url, formats_hash)` only as an adapter-agnostic lookup; after provider selection, PM validates `adapter_id`, discards a mismatched hit, and fetches fresh.
- Cache routing must skip read-time cache for requests with actions, may still store the post-action result, and must preserve PM-cache precedence over Firecrawl cache with diff-reuse audit states.
- Web content caching is per-project with a 500 MB default cache budget, per-operation TTL defaults, LRU eviction for bounded storage, stable cache key ordering, and change detection persistence for later `change_tracking` comparison.
- When `change_tracking: true` and a cached entry exists, even if expired, PM fetches fresh content, compares `content_hash` against the cached entry, returns `change_status: "changed"` with `diff_summary` when content differs, returns `change_status: "same"` and may extend TTL when content matches, and returns `change_status: "removed"` when the previous URL entry existed but the fresh fetch resolves to 404.
